title: Residue tensor intervals under finite-coefficient immersion operations
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites and the coefficient categories $D^b_c(T,A_n)$ and $D^b_c(T,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], for $T=X,Z,U$.
Fix $n\ge1$, set $A=A_n$ and $\kappa=A/(\varpi)$, and use ordinary derived tensor on constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-derived-tensor]. For integers $a\le b$, let Tor amplitude mean vanishing of $\mathcal H^r(C\otimes_A^L M)$ outside $[a,b]$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $M$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The finite operations $i^*,j^*,i_*$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image] preserve bounded constructibility and Tor intervals unchanged. More precisely, for $P\in D^b_c(Z,A)$ the canonical projection map is an isomorphism in the unbounded derived category $D(X_{\rm proet},A)$:
$$i_*P\otimes_A^L\kappa_X\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*(P\otimes_A^L\kappa_Z).$$
For every $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ and each immersion pullback $u=i,j$, its derived monoidal comparison identifies $u^*(K\otimes_A^L\kappa_X)$ with $u^*K\otimes_A^L\kappa_{\operatorname{dom}u}$ and preserves the cohomological interval of this tensor. For $T=X,Z,U$ and every bounded constructible etale $C'$, the comparison pullback $\nu_T^*$ preserves and reflects the interval of $C'\otimes_A^L\kappa$ and therefore preserves and reflects its Tor interval [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. No perfectness assumption on the residue module $\kappa$ is imposed; when $n>1$ it need not be perfect.

source.place: Residue criterion and (3 prime) for immersion operations; returned steps 14–15

proof.text: The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, and its spectrum is a singleton). Hence $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sf-closed-partition-module-test] to the one-stratum partition of $Z$: the complementary open $j$ is quasi-compact. Now [lem-sf-finite-immersion-constructibility-interval] gives bounded constructibility for $i^*,j^*,i_*$. Its hypotheses are Noetherian $X$ and invertibility of $\ell$; its auxiliary global finite-field datum imposes no field-of-definition condition on $X$, so it applies to the present $k$. No integral-stage assertion is needed.

source.place: Finite stage and (3 prime): bounded constructibility

proof.text: On the ambient unbounded categories the immersion inverse images are exact, using [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] and the constant coefficient identifications [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Closed direct image is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Thus $Ri_*=i_*$ termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. For all these exact functors $F$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $\mathcal H^r(FC)=F\mathcal H^r(C)$ for arbitrary complexes, including complexes unbounded below. In particular they preserve every cohomological interval. The same assertion for $\nu_T^*$, together with its constant coefficient identification, is [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact].

source.place: Residue criterion: exactness on arbitrary complexes

proof.text: Apply the unbounded monoidal comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $i,j$, and to $\nu_T$. The coefficient identifications of step 2 apply both to $A$ and to the finite ring $\kappa$; their maps preserve constant sections and therefore the quotient action $A\to\kappa$. Consequently $u^*\kappa=\kappa$, as an $A$-module sheaf, and the canonical comparison gives $u^*(C\otimes_A^L\kappa)\cong u^*C\otimes_A^L\kappa$. Step 2 proves preservation of its cohomological interval for $u=i,j,\nu_T$. These comparisons are valid without a lower bound on $C\otimes_A^L\kappa$.

source.place: Residue criterion: monoidal comparison with the residue sheaf

proof.text: We check the specified projection map, for arbitrary $M\in D(X_{\rm proet},A)$, rather than only $M=\kappa_X$. Write $S=i_*P\otimes_A^LM$ and let $\eta,\varepsilon$ be the unit and counit of $i^*\dashv i_*$. By [lem-weil-proetale-closed-tensor-projection], $S$ is isomorphic to an object in the image of $i_*$. The counit is invertible on the unbounded categories by [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. The triangle identity gives $i_*\varepsilon_D\circ\eta_{i_*D}=1$, so $\eta_{i_*D}$ is invertible; naturality then makes $\eta_S$ invertible. The canonical projection map is precisely the composite $S\xrightarrow{\eta_S}i_*i^*S\xrightarrow{i_*\mu}i_*(i^*i_*P\otimes_A^Li^*M)\xrightarrow{i_*(\varepsilon_P\otimes1)}i_*(P\otimes_A^Li^*M)$: its adjoint is $(\varepsilon_P\otimes1)\mu$. Here $\mu$ is the monoidal comparison of step 3, so every factor is invertible. This proves the asserted canonical isomorphism on taking $M=\kappa_X$.

source.place: (3 prime) for closed pushforward: canonical unbounded projection map

proof.text: If $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, the criterion [lem-sf-proetale-residue-tor-test] gives that $K\otimes_A^L\kappa_X$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$. Its hypothesis is that the scheme has $\ell$ invertible; the auxiliary global finite-field datum only fixes the coefficient ring and imposes no field-of-definition condition on that scheme. By steps 2 and 3, $u^*K\otimes_A^L\kappa\cong u^*(K\otimes_A^L\kappa_X)$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$ for $u=i,j$. By step 1 the object $u^*K$ is bounded constructible. Applying the converse direction of the same residue criterion on $Z$ or $U$ proves Tor amplitude $[a,b]$.

source.place: (3 prime) for the two inverse images: unchanged Tor interval

proof.text: Let $P\in D^b_c(Z,A)$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ and let $M$ be any degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf. In step 4 its pullback $i^*M$ is again a degree-zero module sheaf by step 2. Therefore $P\otimes_A^Li^*M$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$, by the definition of Tor amplitude. The projection isomorphism of step 4 and $\mathcal H^r(i_*D)=i_*\mathcal H^r(D)$ from step 2 show that $i_*P\otimes_A^LM$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$. This holds for every $M$, so $i_*P$ has that Tor interval. Together with step 1 it gives the closed direct-image preservation asserted in the item.

source.place: (3 prime) for closed pushforward: test against every module sheaf

proof.text:
Finally put $B=C'\otimes_A^L\kappa$ on $T_{m et}$; it need not be bounded below. For every integer $r$, exactness gives $\mathcal H^r(
u_T^*B)\cong
u_T^*\mathcal H^r(B)$ by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. If this is zero, apply [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] to the degree-zero object $\mathcal H^r(B)[0]$, which is bounded below regardless of $B$: the isomorphism $\mathcal H^r(B)[0]\cong R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*(\mathcal H^r(B)[0])$ forces $\mathcal H^r(B)=0$. This proves reflection of the interval degree by degree; preservation was step 3. For the Tor interval of bounded constructible $C'$, apply [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] directly to $C'\in D^+$, which tests against all module sheaves on each site. No comparison theorem on unbounded-below $B$ and no perfectness of $\kappa$ has been used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NB-24d6bf27a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no changes. The item is a split of the unsplit Q35 node; it has no new nodes, the statement is unchanged, proof_deps equals the union of uses, there is no SGA citation, and the snapshot has no repair note. Source checked: main-20261015 prop-sf-localization-all-stages.proof.md lines 84-107 (residue criterion and (3') for i^*, j^*, i_*). Steps 1-3: X is Noetherian because it is of finite type over Spec k; every open of a Noetherian X is quasi-compact, so j is quasi-compact (lem-sf-closed-partition-module-test), which the open-closed and projection lemmas require. Constructibility comes from lem-sf-finite-immersion-constructibility-interval, whose global finite-field datum puts no condition on X. Exactness and monoidal comparison for u = i, j, nu_T hold on unbounded complexes, and u^*kappa = kappa compatibly with A -> kappa. Step 4 proves that the canonical projection map is an isomorphism, not just some isomorphism: S lies in the image of i_*, the counit is invertible, and the triangle identity makes eta invertible; the composite is checked to be adjoint to (eps(x)1)mu. Step 5 uses the residue test in both directions; it needs only that ell is invertible on Z and U. Step 6 gets the Tor amplitude of i_*P directly from the definition, testing against every module M via the projection isomorphism and exact i_*. Step 7 correctly repairs the blueprint's bounded-below misuse: for A = Z/4 and kappa = F_2, kappa(x)^L kappa is unbounded below, so reflection is done one degree at a time with thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison applied to H^r(B)[0]; the Tor interval of C' follows from lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval. Edge cases checked: Z or U empty, n = 1, a = b. No duplicate found (checked prop-exc-closed-tor, lem-sf-supported-tor-reduction-propagation and lem-sp-supported-scalar-tor-interval). The 14 generic tool uses are accepted, since the unit's single Hom/adjunction step supplies none of them; their 'why' texts are boilerplate, which is cosmetic.
